Winners: American biologists Mary E. Brunkow and Fred Ramsdell and Japanese biologist Shimon Sakaguchi[1] won the 2025 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. The Karolinska Institutet announced it on October 6, 2025.
Discovery: The prize was for their groundbreaking discoveries concerning peripheral immune tolerance that prevents the immune system from harming the body.[2] The laureates identified the immune system's "security guards," regulatory T cells, thus laying the foundation for a new field of research.[2] These cells stop other T cells from attacking the body's own cells.[1]
Impact: Their discoveries have spurred the development of new treatments, for example for cancer and autoimmune diseases.[2]
